latin: Per deorum cedes tragice a theologis septima unitas discretiua intellectualis ebdomadae designatur.
latin_note: The German-language secondary work cited here as 'kabbalah_paradigma' quotes the thesis with the verb 'designantur' (plural) rather than Farmer's printed 'designatur' (singular) (kabbalah_paradigma:1868); this variant is not otherwise explained in the material consulted.
translation: Through the slaughters of the gods, the theologians tragically signify the seventh, distinguishing unity of the intellectual hebdomad.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch9, from Latin at farmer1998:16157

sources.pico_relation: Farmer cites this passage of Proclus's Platonic Theology as the thesis's source

doctrine: Farmer's note identifies the 'theologians' as the Orphic theologians, and glosses the 'seventh distinguishing unity' as the last of the seven principal henads in what Proclus calls the intellectual hebdomad (farmer1998:16194).
context: Farmer's cross-reference network links the thesis to 22.1-3, 23.2, 24.12, 28.3, and 3>4 (farmer1998:16157).
historiography: The work cited as 'kabbalah_paradigma', whose author the packet marks as unconfirmed, pairs this thesis with the Cabalistic conclusion 11>11 and the Zoroastrian conclusion 8>7 as parallel formulations (kabbalah_paradigma:1868).
not_established: The author of the work cited as 'kabbalah_paradigma' is not confirmed in the material consulted.
Which edition or manuscript underlies the 'designantur' variant is not established by the sources consulted.
